insight.title: What keeps the world in perfect motion
insight.subtitle: A quiet look at the invisible threads that bind our days together.

sections.text: Look at the objects around you. Your ceramic mug, the soft light from a bulb, the linen of your shirt. None of these arrived by chance. Behind every quiet moment lies a vast, invisible river of human effort and precision. We live inside a masterpiece of coordination that we rarely stop to see.

The world breathes through a hidden pulse of movement. Ships cross oceans while you sleep, and currents of electricity flow like water beneath your feet. It is a silent choreography of gears, code, and care. Everything is held together by millions of small, intentional choices made by people you will never meet.

Understanding this system changes how you see the street outside. You are part of a living tapestry where every thread matters. When things work, they feel like magic. But the real beauty is the harmony. It is the steady, quiet promise that we are all looking after one another, even in the dark.

news.title: Government Enforces Restrictions on Precious Metal Imports to Curb FTA Misuse
news.description: The government has imposed new import restrictions on gold, platinum, and silver jewellery to prevent misuse of Free Trade Agreements. Importers now require a license from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade. Exemptions exist for 100% Export-Oriented Units and certain foreign trade policy schemes.

news.title: US-India Trade Tensions: Satellite Preferences and Internet Shutdowns Spotlighted
news.description: The US has flagged India's domestic satellite preference for DTH services and localised internet shutdowns as barriers to foreign trade in its 2026 report. These practices are seen as limiting market access for foreign companies and impeding the digital economy, urging India to pursue a more open policy.

news.title: "Nothing says 'America First' like launching war for foreign regime": Iran FM Araghchi slams US over conflict
news.description: In a post on X on Tuesday, Araghchi criticised the US policy of 'America First', if it meant, according to him, the reason for the ongoing conflict and also a way to 'earn profits', while the casualties of the war, according to him, will be 'young soldiers'.
